summary.pack_description:
Collect 3 highlights celebrating the 2017 Dallas Stars draft picks with the 2017 Draft Discoveries Pack! Created in collaboration with the Dallas Stars, these new highlights celebrate exciting playoff moments from the developing legacies of Jake Oettinger, Jason Robertson, and Miro Heiskanen.

This commemorative collection is being released on June 28 – the first day of the 2024 NHL Draft!

Each pack contains 2 mystery highlights that could be either Miro Heiskanen’s first career playoff game-winning goal in Game 6 of the 2022 Western Conference Quarterfinals (Limited #/500), Jason Robertson’s mid-air tap-in game-tying goal in Game 4 of the 2023 Western Conference Final (Core #/1500), or Jake Oettinger’s lead-preserving save in Game 4 of the 2023 Western Conference Quarterfinals (Core #/1500).

release.name: 2017 Draft Discoveries Pack
release.description:
Sale Starts: Friday June 28, 2024 at 12pm CT / 1pm ET / 10am PT

 

Price: $7 USD

# Packs Available: 1,750. Edition numbers are distributed randomly.

 

Purchase Limit: Ten (10) pack limit per person for the first 24 hours; limit increased to thirty (30) pack limit per person afterwards. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 2

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • Two (2) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 42.9% Jake Oettinger’s save in Game 4 of the 2023 Western Conference Quarterfinals (Core #/1500)
    • 42.9% Jason Robertson’s first goal in Game 4 of the 2023 Western Conference Final (Core #/1500)
    • 14.3% Miro Heiskanen’s first career playoff game-winning goal in Game 6 of the 2022 Western Conference Quarterfinals (Limited #/500)

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be made via registered payment processor MoonPay where available; where not available, payments will be processed via Stripe.

 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights are eligible to be sold to other collectors in the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace. See FAQ.

 

Transferability: Packs and highlights can be exchanged in the Trade Lounge™ with other NHL Breakaway users.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

 

Sets Included:

  • Hometown History: Dallas Stars, Series 1 - Preview

 

Collection Guarantee: Series 1 highlights will only be distributed during Series 1, which ends ~September 2024. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

 

All sales subject to Terms

summary.name: Jake Oettinger
summary.description:
With the Stars holding a 3-2 lead in the closing seconds of Game 4 in their first-round series against Minnesota at Xcel Energy Center on April 23, 2023, goaltender Jake Oettinger delivered a highlight-reel save on Wild forward Marcus Johansson. Oettinger was able to push from right to left to rob Johansson, who was all alone at the right faceoff circle. Oettinger's glove save preserved the lead for Dallas, who won the game to tie the series at 2-2.

summary.name: Jason Robertson
summary.description:
Proving he can score in a multitude of ways, Stars forward Jason Robertson used some nifty hand-eye coordination to get Dallas on the board in Game 4 of the Western Conference Final vs. Vegas at American Airlines Center on May 25, 2023. After Golden Knights goaltender Adin Hill made the initial stop on Robertson, the puck popped out of his glove, allowing Robertson to tap it to his forehand in mid-air. It was his first of two goals in the contest - both game-tying markers - in a game the Stars won 3-2 in overtime.

summary.name: Miro Heiskanen
summary.description:
In a 2-2 tie with less than three minutes remaining in the second period of Game 6 of Dallas' first-round matchup with Calgary at American Airlines Center on May 13, 2022, Stars defenseman Miro Heiskanen showcased his offensive flair to score the go-ahead goal and eventual game winner to force Game 7. Receiving a pass just inside the blueline, Heiskanen deked Flames forward Matthew Tkachuk and cut back towards the middle, giving him the time and space needed to fire off a shot that sailed through traffic and past goaltender Jacob Markstrom.
